sections.content: A time word can start the sentence or end it, and the meaning stays the same: *Esta mañana hemos visitado el mercado* and *Hemos visitado el mercado esta mañana*. At the start, no comma is needed. The verb group stays together: never put the time word between *haber* and the participle.

items.spanish: Esta mañana hemos visitado el mercado.
items.english: This morning we have visited the market.

items.spanish: Hemos visitado el mercado esta mañana.
items.english: We have visited the market this morning.

items.spanish: Hoy hemos descansado en la terraza.
items.english: Today we have rested on the terrace.

items.spanish: Hemos descansado en la terraza hoy.
items.english: We have rested on the terrace today.

sections.content: Start with the time word when you want to say when first; end with it when the news comes first. Both are correct.
